record.question: What is the important principle and use of frozen section in histopatholgy?
options: To quickly preserve tissue in the natural state
To quickly obtain sections for diagnosis without processing in paraffin
record.explanation: Answer B: To quickly obtain sections for diagnosis without processing in paraffin. Frozen sectioning provides rapid intraoperative tissue diagnosis without routine dehydration, clearing, and paraffin infiltration. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430685/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
